claims.text: The starting cast CoCrFeMnNi-based alloy has coarse grains greater than 100 µm.
The starting cast alloy has limited ductility.
The starting CoCrFeMnNi alloy is single-phase FCC.
Adding 0.5-1.0 at.% Al permits formation of an FCC+BCC solid-solution constitution while suppressing complex phases.
Room-temperature HPT or ECAP followed by annealing at 400-600°C for 10-30 minutes will produce a stable nanocrystalline FCC+BCC microstructure below 50 nm.
A deformation strain greater than 4.0 and annealing for less than one hour are sufficient to avoid excessive grain coarsening.
Dislocation-cell substructures created by severe plastic deformation act as BCC-phase nucleation sites.
A high grain-boundary density and solute drag from Cr, Mn, or Al inhibit grain growth.
Grain-boundary density and solute drag suppress diffusion-controlled sigma- and Laves-phase formation.
Local lattice distortion and stored deformation energy drive an FCC-to-BCC transformation.
Solute segregation at grain boundaries stabilizes grain sizes below 50 nm.
Nanocrystalline grains and FCC/BCC phase boundaries increase strength through Hall-Petch and phase-boundary strengthening.
Avoiding long-range ordered intermetallics prevents catastrophic brittle fracture.
The processed alloy will have equiaxed grains averaging 20-45 nm.
The processed alloy will contain 5-15 vol% BCC material uniformly dispersed in an FCC matrix.
The processed alloy will have yield strength above 1.2 GPa while retaining measurable ductility.
As-cast equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi has a yield strength of approximately 200-300 MPa.
The low strength and limited ductility of the cast baseline result from macro-segregation and insufficient grain-boundary strengthening.
Annealing above 700°C causes grain growth beyond 100 nm and nucleation of brittle sigma or Laves phases.
Al contents above 1.5 at.% without sufficient Mn destabilize the dual-phase structure and produce an entirely brittle BCC structure.

contradictions.description: The conditions specify atmospheric pressure, whereas HPT intrinsically requires application of high compressive pressure. Ambient external atmosphere could still apply, but the stated pressure condition is internally ambiguous or incompatible with the HPT option.
